newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends firmer, traders await Iraq.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends firmer, traders await Iraq.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures ended slightly firmer on Thursday and traders said markets were directionless for most of the day in the absence of any important fresh news about long-awaited Iraqi oil exports.
September Brent crude closed three cents a barrel firmer at $18.42 after jumping as high as $18.50 just before the close.
August gas oil closed just 25 cents firmer in the afternoon at $165.25.
"Nothing really new. Gasoline was fairly strong and that took the WTI (NYMEX crude) through a couple of stops, and Brent came up a bit with that," one IPE broker said.
"Once the paper buying had eased off it came back down again," one broker said.
Iraqi oil sales under a U.N. oil-for-food deal have been delayed while the U.N. considers Baghdad's aid distribution plan.

The $2 billion six-month deal which came into effect on June 8 has been split into two three-month, $1 billion tranches and members of the U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq said on Thursday Baghdad would not be allowed to change deadlines for the first tranche.
Baghdad will also not be allowed to carry over more than five percent of its oil allocation from the first tranche into the second, the U.N. has said.

Industry analysts suggest this means Iraq will have to squeeze out 1.5 - 2 million barrels per day whe exports resume, possibly in mid-August, in order to meet its $1 billion cash target by early September.
